pages.title: About POPS | First Order of Protection
pages.text: The Doctrine Protect the Record. Preserve the Truth. P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System is not a support group. It is a support machine. It was built for the father who is being denied access to his child and needs to move through the system with discipline, proof, and restraint. The Doctrine POPS is not a support group. It is a support machine. It was built for the father who is being denied access to his child and needs to move through the system with discipline, proof, and restraint. Not panic. Not revenge. Not desperation. A record. POPS exists because when a father's presence is questioned, emotion is not enough. Memory is not enough. Pain is not enough. The record has to stand. The Mission There is a place in a father that does not need to be taught. The instinct to protect. The duty to stand between harm and the child. The responsibility to show up, provide, guard, and remain accountable even when nobody is watching. That duty is not created by a court order. It is older than that. It lives in conscience, in blood, in faith, and in the charge placed inside a man to protect what has been entrusted to him. So when a father is separated from his child, that calling does not disappear. It becomes trapped. He is still a protector, but the door is locked. He is still responsible, but his hands are tied. He is still called a father, but treated like a visitor. He still carries the duty, but is denied the place to perform it. POPS was built for that place. Not to attack. Not to inflame. Not to spy. Not to turn pain into revenge. POPS exists to help a father preserve the truth when the truth is being contested. The Four Pillars Presence Presence is not just standing in a place. Presence is the call made, the message sent, the arrival at the exchange, the request for records, the follow-up after silence, and the lawful attempt when the door does not open. POPS is designed to help preserve a record of those attempts for later review. Protection Protection means guarding the child, the truth, the record, and the lawful path forward. Not aggression. Not intimidation. Not chaos. Discipline. Standing watch over the facts. Proof A painful story is not enough in court. A pattern needs structure. An event needs a date. A claim needs evidence. A file needs a hash. A timeline needs custody. A report needs restraint. POPS turns scattered facts into organized proof. Restraint Pain can make a person speak in ways that hurt their own case. POPS does not erase the pain. It preserves the original words, then helps translate the record into court-safe language. The truth stays strong without becoming reckless. How the System Thinks POPS follows a disciplined six-step product direction. The steps below describe intended behavior; extraction, sealing, custody logs, and report outputs require verification against the release supplied. The application organizes user-provided information and does not independently verify events. Capture Record what happened or upload a document, image, message export, receipt, court order, photo, screenshot, or other evidence. Preserve The original file is copied into protected local storage and hashed with SHA-256 so the system can later verify whether it changed. Extract When possible, POPS reads documents, images, screenshots, message exports, and court records to pull out dates, times, names, messages, case numbers, order language, and event details automatically. Review The system presents what it found. The user reviews, corrects, and confirms. POPS does not silently replace the user's judgment. Seal Once confirmed, the record is sealed, hashed, logged, and preserved in the Evidence Vault and audit ledger. Report The system helps generate timelines, evidence indexes, chain-of-custody reports, hash verification reports, attorney packets, and court-safe summaries. The goal is simple: when it is time to speak, the user does not walk in with scattered fragments. He walks in with a record. The Promise Every attempt matters. Every lawful effort matters. Every message matters. Every date matters. Every piece of evidence deserves protection. POPS is not a lawyer. It is not therapy. It is not a social network. It is not a revenge tool. It is not a surveillance system. It does not guarantee admissibility. POPS is a disciplined evidence system. It helps a parent say: I showed up. I tried. I stayed lawful. I preserved the evidence. I documented the truth. When presence is questioned, the record speaks. Built for the Hardest Days This app is built for the parking lot after a missed exchange. The unanswered message. The medical appointment learned about too late. The school record no one sent. The court order nobody seems to follow. The receipt that proves the trip was made. The screenshot that needs context. The long thread that shows the pattern. The quiet moment where a man wonders if anyone will ever believe how hard he tried. POPS does not pretend that pain is small. It does not tell a father to stop feeling what he feels. It gives him something better to do with it. It gives the pain a disciplined path. It gives the protector a post to stand at again. Technical Foundation POPS is built as a local-first evidence workstation. The desktop app is designed around local records, local storage, and user-controlled export. Evidence files are preserved, hashed with SHA-256, and connected to timelines, incidents, court orders, communications, and reports. Product direction — availability requires release verification: Local SQLite record storage Evidence preservation SHA-256 file verification Chain-of-custody logging Court-safe summaries Attorney packet exports Hash verification reports Structured timeline building Document and image extraction where possible Encrypted backup and export paths as the security layer matures POPS is built to be auditable, portable, and court-friendly. The local-first design aims to keep records under user control. Specific network behavior, backup, encryption, and export features must be confirmed for the supplied release. Proof of Presence Protect the record. Preserve the truth.

pages.text: One fictional example • Five practical steps From a difficult moment to a record you can review. This walkthrough follows Alex, a fictional father documenting an exchange that did not take place. The example explains the intended workflow without claiming that a demonstration is a real case or proof of an event. Release clarity Steps describe the product workflow. Exact screens, supported file types, integrity checks, and export functions depend on the tested release. Actual release captures will be added after verification. 1. Capture what you personally observed Alex starts with the scheduled exchange date, the agreed place, and a short factual note about what happened. A useful entry separates the planned event from the observed result. It avoids guessing about another person's motives or turning a disagreement into a legal conclusion. The benefit is context while the details are fresh. Instead of returning weeks later to reconstruct a confusing afternoon, Alex has an identifiable event to review. If a detail is uncertain, the note should say so rather than invent precision. Use fictional records while learning the software. The website beta form is for contact and platform information, not for submitting the exchange details or the supporting evidence. 2. Keep supporting material and its source context Alex associates a harmless example message and receipt with the event. Source notes explain where each item came from and whether it is an original export, screenshot, or other copy. A screenshot can be useful without being equivalent to the underlying source record. Where supported by the release, file hashing creates a reference fingerprint for later comparison. It can help identify a change in file contents. It does not establish that Alex was at a location or that the account of the exchange is true. Original-file preservation, metadata retention, and custody logging must be verified before relying on a specific build. Keep independent source material and appropriate backups. 3. Connect the pieces in a chronology Alex connects the event with its supporting files and relevant order reference. The timeline gives the event a place among other dated records. That makes it easier to find the right material when preparing for a discussion. Organization is useful even when a record is incomplete. A missing attachment or uncertain date should remain visible as a gap. The software should not be presented as filling gaps with independently verified facts. The Windows workspace is the primary product. Mobile capture and Windows–Android synchronization are forthcoming work; this example does not depend on an announced synchronization feature. 4. Review the record before interpreting it Alex reads the event in sequence, checks the attached material, and corrects any inaccurate notes. Dates, source labels, names, and the distinction between observation and inference all matter. A repeated sequence can prompt a question without establishing a legal finding. The practical benefit is a clearer starting point for review. A lawyer can ask about a specific event and its source context instead of receiving an unexplained collection of images. P.O.P.S. does not replace that professional judgment. pages.title: The POPS Declaration | First Order of Protection
pages.text: Proof of Presence System The P.O.P.S. Declaration First Order of Protection and Service Mission Statement POPS - the Proof of Presence System - exists to restore men to their God-given appointment as the First Order of Protection in the home. It equips fathers with the discipline, record-keeping, and truth-preserving tools needed to stand watch over their families, remain accountable in conflict, and protect what has been entrusted to them. POPS strengthens the man, safeguards the record, and preserves the truth when presence is questioned, challenged, or denied. POPS is not a support group. It is a support machine - built to keep a man aligned, sober-minded, and anchored to his calling, even in the hardest seasons of fatherhood. About This Declaration The P.O.P.S. Declaration is the foundational document of the First Order of Protection. It is not a policy, a slogan, or a motivational speech. It is the formal articulation of what men have always been in the home: the first responder, the first defender, the first witness, and the first line of protection long before institutions existed. This Declaration defines the charge, the duty, and the office of the father - not as a cultural role, but as a God-given appointment. It affirms the rights, responsibilities, and presence of the man who stands between his family and the dark, and calls that role by its true name: P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System. Preamble When in the course of a family's life, danger does not announce itself, when the call for help cannot wait for sirens, when the wolf is at the door and the door is the only thing between the wolf and the children, there must stand, in that gap, a man. Not a badge. Not a uniform. A father. Before there were Courts of Protection Services, before there were County Officers of Public Safety, before any institution wore the name of guardian, there was the man of the house, standing watch, armed with nothing but resolve and the authority given to him by his Creator. We call this what it has always been: P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System. The First Order of Protection and Service. This is not a replacement for law. This is the foundation law was built upon. When the C.O.P.S. cannot get there in time, and there will be moments they cannot, the P.O.P.S. is already there. He was never not there. That is the whole of the charge. We hold these truths to be self-evident, God-given, and undeniable: that every father is entrusted with rights, privileges, and responsibilities that no government granted and no government may revoke; that presence is not passive but is itself a duty; and that a man who stands watch over his household stands in an office older than nations. The Articles Article I On the Origin of the Charge The duty of a man to protect his household is not granted by any government, council, or institution of man. It precedes them all. It was given at the founding of the family itself, and it answers to a higher authority than any badge or statute. What the State formalizes as protective services, the home has always practiced as the first and oldest service of all. Article II On the Nature of Presence Protection is not an event. It is a condition. A man does not become a protector in the moment of crisis. He either was one in every ordinary moment before it, or he was not. Proof of Presence is not proof that he showed up when it mattered. It is proof that he never left. Article III On the Limits of Outside Help We do not despise the C.O.P.S. We honor them, we call them, we cooperate with them. But we do not outsource the charge to them. There is a gap between the call and the arrival, between the danger and the response, and in that gap a family is either covered or it is not. The P.O.P.S. exists in that gap. Always has. Always will. Article IV On Rights Inseparable from Responsibility The right to protect one's household is inseparable from the responsibility to do so. A right not exercised becomes a duty unmet. We claim no privilege we are not also prepared to discharge in full: in vigilance, in provision, in defense, and in sacrifice if it is asked of us. Article V On Record and Witness What is unrecorded is too easily denied, and what is undefended is too easily forgotten. The P.O.P.S. system exists not to glorify the watchman, but to ensure that his presence, his diligence, his decisions, and his care can be proven when proof is needed. Truth protected. Evidence verified. Integrity that does not depend on anyone's memory but stands on its own record. Article VI On the Permanence of the Office Titles change. Employers change. Circumstances change. The office of protector, once accepted, does not retire, resign, or expire. A man may lay down many things in life. This is not one of them. Filed under the authority of every man who has ever stood between his family and the dark, and called it nothing more than Tuesday. From Philosophy to Practice Proof of Presence requires a record. The P.O.P.S. Declaration establishes the standard. The desktop application helps preserve evidence, organize timelines, verify files with SHA-256 integrity, and prepare a court-safe record for attorney review. Get P.O.P.S.

pages.title: The POPS Pledge | Preserve Protect Prove
pages.text: First Order of Protection The Creed & The Pledge Preserve. Protect. Prove. The Creed The Charge I am the First Order of Protection. Before the law arrives, I am here. Before the danger is named, I am watching. Before my family asks, I have already decided: I will not fail them. I do not wait for permission to protect what is mine. I do not require a title to fulfill a calling. My badge is my presence. My oath was sworn the day I accepted this house as my charge. I will preserve what has been entrusted to me. I will protect those who cannot yet protect themselves. I will prove, by action, not by word, that the watchman did not sleep. Preserve Protect Prove This is not a slogan. This is the order of operations for every day I am given breath. The Pledge of Commitment I make this pledge not to an institution, but to the ones under my roof, and before the God who placed them in my care. Presence I pledge my presence: that I will be found, that I will be reachable, that I will not be a stranger in my own home. Vigilance I pledge my vigilance: that I will see the danger before it announces itself, and act before I am asked. Readiness I pledge my readiness: that whatever the moment requires, I will not be found unprepared, untrained, or unwilling. Record I pledge my record: that my actions will speak, and that if ever questioned, the proof of what I did and when I did it will stand on its own. Restraint I pledge my restraint: that my strength exists to shield, not to dominate; my authority exists to serve, not to rule. Permanence I pledge my permanence: that this charge does not end at the end of a shift, a season, or a hard year. It ends when I do, and not before. This is the First Order. This is Proof of Presence. From Philosophy to Practice Proof of Presence requires a record. The P.O.P.S. Pledge establishes the commitment. The desktop application helps preserve evidence, organize timelines, verify files with SHA-256 integrity, and prepare a court-safe record for attorney review. Get P.O.P.S.

pages.title: POPS Lexicon | Court-Safe Evidence Language
pages.text: Court Language Guide POPS Lexicon Plain-English courtroom terms, evidence language, and factual rewrite guidance for parents building disciplined records. Core Court Terms POPS helps users recognize courtroom language, understand it in plain English, and preserve facts in a clear, organized way. This guide is educational. It can help you understand terms you may encounter in court documents, hearings, attorney conversations, or case records. It does not replace legal advice or determine what should be filed in court. Rewrite guidance: Prefer facts over conclusions. Prefer dates, records, and actions over blame. Prefer documented events over legal labels. Search the POPS Lexicon Showing 10 of 10 terms · Court-safe explanations · Educational only All Terms High Sensitivity Evidence Court Procedure Constitutional Legal culpable High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Legally or morally responsible for wrongdoing. Why it matters: This word can sound like a legal conclusion, so POPS should encourage factual wording instead of blame. POPS use: Flag for attorney review if used in a report, packet, or filing. Court-safe example: The records show the scheduled parenting time did not occur on the dates listed. Open direct definition → Evidence exculpatory Medium Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Evidence that may help show a person did not do something wrong or did comply with an order. Why it matters: Users should be able to tag records that may help show lawful conduct or a good-faith effort. POPS use: Allow tagging and evidence classification. Court-safe example: This message may be exculpatory because it shows I appeared at the exchange location on time. Open direct definition → Court Procedure pro se Medium Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Representing yourself in court without an attorney. Why it matters: Many POPS users may be self-represented and need organizing help. POPS use: Show as informational and supportive, not as legal advice. Court-safe example: I am appearing pro se and have organized the attached records for the Court's review. Open direct definition → Legal Standard prima facie High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Something that appears sufficient on its face unless challenged by other evidence. Why it matters: This is a legal threshold term and should be used carefully. POPS use: Flag for review when used as a conclusion. Court-safe example: The timeline and records may show a prima facie pattern of missed parenting time. Open direct definition → Legal Doctrine estoppel High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: A rule that may prevent someone from taking a position that conflicts with earlier words, actions, or promises when another person relied on them. Why it matters: POPS should preserve messages, agreements, and reliance evidence. POPS use: Flag for attorney review if used in a filing. Court-safe example: The messages show an agreed exchange time, and I relied on that agreement by appearing at the location. Open direct definition → Constitutional Procedure habeas corpus High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: "You shall have the body." A procedure used to challenge unlawful detention or restraint. Why it matters: This is a serious legal procedure and should be handled cautiously. POPS use: Restrict to informational display and attorney review guidance. Court-safe example: This term involves serious legal procedure and should be reviewed with an attorney or appropriate legal authority before use. Open direct definition → Constitutional Right Fifth Amendment High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: A constitutional protection that includes due process and protection against self-incrimination. Why it matters: Statements involving accusations, police contact, admissions, or investigations may need careful review. POPS use: Flag sensitive narrative content for review. Court-safe example: Statements involving possible criminal exposure should be reviewed by counsel before filing or sharing. Open direct definition → Fourteenth Amendment High Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: A constitutional protection that includes due process and equal protection principles. Why it matters: In family-law contexts, users may hear this discussed in relation to notice, hearings, fairness, and state action. POPS use: Provide plain-language explanation and flag constitutional claims for review. Court-safe example: My records are organized to show notice received, appearances made, and communication attempts. Open direct definition → Constitutional Principle due process Medium Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: Fair legal procedure, including notice and an opportunity to be heard before important rights are affected. Why it matters: POPS can help track service, hearings, filings, and procedural gaps. POPS use: Support factual tracking; do not suggest legal conclusions. Court-safe example: The attached records show the dates I received notice and the steps I took to respond. Open direct definition → equal protection Medium Sensitivity Plain-English meaning: The idea that the government should apply the law fairly and not treat similarly situated people differently without a lawful reason. Why it matters: POPS should preserve facts and comparisons for attorney review. POPS use: Keep factual and avoid encouraging unsupported constitutional claims. Court-safe example: The records show the dates, actions taken, and how the situation was handled compared with prior events. Open direct definition → Use this guide to understand a term—not to make a legal conclusion. Start with the plain-English meaning. Preserve the facts. Use dates, records, messages, and actions instead of labels or accusations.

pages.text: POPS PRIVACY Privacy and Operational Notice What POPS handles, what stays under the user's control, and what should never be sent through general website forms. 1. Privacy Principle POPS is designed around a local-first principle: family records should remain under the user's control unless the user deliberately chooses to export, share, upload, submit, or transmit them. The POPS website and the POPS desktop application serve different functions. The website is a public information, support, and access channel. The desktop application is intended to help users organize their own case records locally. POPS does not promise automatic cloud backup, encrypted storage, attorney sharing, permanent evidence preservation, or remote access unless a specific active product feature clearly states that it is enabled and explains how it works. 2. Information POPS May Receive POPS may receive information that a person voluntarily enters through a website form, purchase process, account process, support request, Open Door Access request, or Noted Counsel submission. 2.1 Information You May Provide Name, email address, and contact message Purchase, license, or access-request information Support questions and product-feedback information Open Door Access information necessary to review an access request Noted Counsel Merit Recognition information submitted for review 2.2 Basic Technical Information Website hosting, security, email, payment, and analytics providers may process limited technical information needed to deliver the website, prevent abuse, maintain security, diagnose technical problems, or measure basic site performance. This may include information such as browser type, device type, IP address, page request information, timestamps, and referral source. POPS does not use this information to build profiles about a user's private family case, child, court matter, medical situation, or legal dispute. 3. Information POPS Does Not Request Through General Forms Do not send private case evidence through a general POPS contact form, social-media message, ordinary support email, Open Door request, or Noted Counsel submission. Unless POPS provides a clearly identified secure process, do not send: Child names, birth dates, addresses, or school identifiers Case numbers, court orders, pleadings, or attorney work product Medical records, school records, or therapy information Private texts, emails, screenshots, audio, video, or evidence files Passwords, account credentials, Social Security numbers, or bank information Emergency information or information requiring immediate legal action POPS may delete, redact, decline to process, or request removal of sensitive information submitted through an inappropriate channel. 4. Local Application Records POPS is intended to help users organize timelines, communications, evidence references, incident notes, court-order details, and reports on their own device. Users remain responsible for protecting their device, operating-system account, passwords, exported files, backups, and any information they choose to share with an attorney, court, advocate, family member, cloud provider, or another person. 4.1 Export Is a User Decision When POPS provides an export or report feature, the user decides what to export and where to send it. POPS does not control, monitor, retrieve, or delete files after they leave the user's device or are shared with another person or service. 4.2 Do Not Assume a Feature Exists The specific POPS release in use controls which storage, backup, file, hash, export, sharing, and security functions are actually available. Users should review the active product documentation before relying on a feature for sensitive records. 5. How POPS Uses Information POPS may use information it receives to: Operate and maintain the website and product-access processes Respond to support, purchase, and licensing requests Issue receipts, licenses, updates, and service communications Review Open Door Access requests under the published program rules Review and moderate Noted Counsel Merit Recognition submissions Prevent fraud, abuse, duplicate submissions, or security threats Meet legal, accounting, tax, recordkeeping, or compliance obligations Improve reliability, accessibility, and product clarity 6. Open Door Access Privacy Open Door Access is a hardship-access path. POPS seeks to collect only the information reasonably needed to review the request, prevent abuse, track reserve availability, and issue an approved license. Applicants should not be required to disclose private court facts, child medical information, evidence, screenshots, or detailed personal trauma to request hardship access. Open Door Access decisions are based on available reserve capacity and program rules. They are not a judgment about a person's worth, parenthood, legal case, or hardship. 7. POPS Noted Counsel Privacy POPS Noted Counsel submissions are private until reviewed. Only a POPS Noted User with a direct first-hand experience may submit a Merit Recognition. POPS may publish only a privacy-safe, edited commendation that the user authorized for publication. POPS may remove names, dates, locations, case details, and other identifying information before publication. 7.1 Positive-Only Merit Recognition POPS Noted Counsel is a curated positive-only Merit Recognition program. It is not a complete review database, public complaint forum, ranking system, referral service, paid attorney directory, or guarantee of legal quality or case results. POPS does not publish star ratings, negative reviews, case accusations, private attorney-client communications, child information, court records, or claims that an attorney guaranteed an outcome. 7.2 No Payment for Recognition Attorneys may not pay for recognition, placement, priority, visibility, commendations, or POPS user introductions. POPS Noted Users may not be paid, pressured, coached, or rewarded for submitting a Merit Recognition. 8. Sharing and Disclosure POPS does not sell or rent personal information or private case information. POPS may share limited information only when reasonably necessary: With service providers that operate hosting, email, payment, security, or support systems When the user expressly authorizes a requested transmission or action To prevent fraud, abuse, security threats, or unlawful activity To comply with a valid legal obligation, subpoena, court order, or legal process To protect the rights, safety, property, or operations of POPS, users, or others POPS does not share a user's local case records unless the user takes an action that deliberately exports, uploads, or shares those records through an available feature. 9. Security Limits POPS uses reasonable operational safeguards appropriate to the active website and product release. No website, device, email system, internet connection, browser, cloud provider, payment processor, or software product can guarantee absolute security. Users should use strong passwords, protect their device, keep software updated, preserve original records where possible, maintain appropriate backups, and avoid sending sensitive family information through unapproved channels. 10. Retention and Deletion POPS retains website, support, access, license, payment-confirmation, fraud-prevention, and operational records only as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose they were collected, subject to legal, accounting, security, and contractual obligations. A person may request correction or deletion of personal information they submitted directly to POPS, subject to applicable obligations and legitimate recordkeeping needs. POPS cannot delete information stored on a user's own device, browser, email account, cloud drive, downloaded export, attorney's records, court filing, or any service outside POPS control. 11. Children POPS is intended for adults, including parents, guardians, attorneys, advocates, and other authorized adults. POPS is not intended for children to create accounts, submit forms, purchase licenses, or use public POPS services. Users should use the minimum child-identifying information necessary for lawful documentation and should protect that information carefully. 12. Changes and Privacy Contact POPS may update this Privacy and Operational Notice as the product, website, security practices, service providers, or legal requirements change. Material changes will be posted with a revised effective date. For privacy questions, correction requests, deletion requests, or Noted Counsel concerns, contact POPS through the privacy contact listed in the site footer. Do not include case evidence, child-identifying information, court documents, medical records, passwords, or emergency details in your first privacy-contact message.

pages.title: POPS Policies and Procedures | Operating Standards
pages.text: POPS GOVERNANCE Policies and Procedures Clear operating standards for Proof of Presence System, Open Door Access, evidence organization, and POPS Noted Counsel. 1. Purpose and Operating Doctrine P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System - helps parents organize facts, preserve records, document good-faith effort, and prepare clearer materials for attorney or court review. POPS is not a law firm. POPS does not provide legal advice, legal representation, legal strategy, or a guarantee of any court result, attorney acceptance, evidence admissibility, or case outcome. 1.1 Core Principle Turn emotion into facts. Turn facts into organized proof. Turn proof into a clearer case file. 1.2 Product Boundary POPS is built to help a parent document what happened, identify the supporting record, organize chronology, and prepare materials for review. It is not built to attack another parent, create revenge material, spy on anyone, or tell a user what legal action to take. 2. Acceptable Use Policy Users must use POPS lawfully, honestly, and with respect for the privacy and rights of others. 2.1 Prohibited Uses Creating, altering, fabricating, or misrepresenting evidence Using POPS to stalk, intimidate, threaten, harass, or retaliate Accessing another person's device, account, or private records without permission Uploading or sharing private information through unapproved channels Using POPS as a substitute for emergency services or qualified legal counsel Presenting POPS-generated material as legal advice, a court order, or verified fact without review 3. Evidence and Record Integrity Procedure POPS helps users organize records. The user remains responsible for the accuracy, completeness, source, and lawful possession of every record they enter, attach, export, or share. 3.1 Preserve Originals Where Possible Users should preserve original messages, native exports, documents, photos, receipts, call logs, and other source material where possible. Screenshots may be useful reference copies, but they can lack source metadata and should not be treated as automatically equivalent to an original record. 3.2 Factual Entry Standard Incident, communication, timeline, and evidence entries should state what occurred, when it occurred, who was involved, what supporting record exists, and what the user personally did. Users should avoid insults, speculation, unsupported accusations, and emotional conclusions. 3.3 User Review Before Export Before exporting or sharing a report, packet, timeline, or statement, the user must review it for accuracy, privacy, completeness, and relevance. POPS does not independently verify the truth of a user's records. 4. Privacy and Operational Boundary POPS is designed around a local-first principle: a parent's family records should remain under that parent's control unless they deliberately choose to export, share, upload, or submit something through a feature that clearly states it will transmit information. 4.1 Do Not Send Private Case Evidence Through General Forms General POPS contact, support, Open Door, and Noted Counsel forms are not for court orders, child names, medical records, school records, screenshots, private messages, audio, video, passwords, Social Security numbers, financial information, or evidence files unless POPS specifically provides a secure purpose-built upload process. 4.2 User Device Responsibility Users are responsible for securing their device, protecting passwords, protecting downloaded reports, maintaining backups where available, and choosing carefully before sharing records with an attorney, court, advocate, or another person. 5. Standard License and Open Door Access The standard POPS license is a one-time purchase of $99.00 . POPS does not require a monthly subscription for the standard license. 5.1 Open Door Access Reserve From every cleared full-price POPS license, 15% - $14.85 - is reserved for Open Door Access. Open Door Access exists to help parents facing real hardship obtain POPS through a Pay What You Can path when reserve funding is available. 5.2 Open Door Rules Applicants must make a non-zero Pay What You Can contribution. That contribution is credited toward the internal Open Door access allowance. The maximum internal allowance for one supported-access license is $99.88 . The Open Door Reserve may cover the difference between the user's contribution and the $99.88 internal allowance, subject to available funds. Open Door Access is limited, reviewed privately, and is not guaranteed. POPS may pause or limit approvals when the reserve cannot responsibly support additional licenses. Refunds, reversals, or chargebacks may reduce the available reserve by the corresponding amount. 5.3 Future Legal Access Extension Open Door Access is the first priority of the reserve. If the reserve grows beyond active Open Door needs and operational obligations, POPS may later establish a separate Legal Access Extension. Potential future uses may include limited legal-consultation support, filing-fee assistance, contributions to qualifying legal-access efforts, or other parent-access resources. No future legal-access program will begin without separately published eligibility rules, funding limits, and procedures. Legal Access Extension support will never be tied to an attorney's placement, recognition, lead, referral, fee, or legal outcome. 6. POPS Noted Counsel - Merit Recognition POPS Noted Counsel is a curated, positive-only merit-recognition program. It exists to recognize attorneys who made a meaningful positive impression on a POPS user through professionalism, honesty, preparation, respectful service, clear communication, or practical help. 6.1 No Rank. No Referral. Only Merit. Noted Counsel is positive-only merit recognition submitted only by POPS Noted Users - not attorneys. There are no rankings, stars, scores, paid placements, self-nominations, referral arrangements, or negative-review forums. 6.2 What POPS Noted Counsel Is Not Not an attorney ranking system Not a referral service or lead-generation program Not a paid attorney directory Not an endorsement of an attorney for a particular legal matter Not a promise that an attorney will accept a case or achieve a result Not a public complaint board or attorney-review battlefield 6.3 Who May Submit a Merit Recognition Only a POPS Noted User may submit a Merit Recognition. A POPS Noted User is a verified POPS user in good standing who has personally had a direct, first-hand experience with the attorney being recognized. The submitting user must confirm that the statement is truthful to the best of their knowledge and that they were not paid, pressured, coached, or rewarded by the attorney, law firm, POPS, or anyone else for the submission. 6.4 What May Be Recognized Professionalism and respectful treatment Clear explanation of options, costs, and limits Honesty and realistic communication Preparedness and organized handling of materials Practical use of a POPS timeline, record set, or attorney packet Responsiveness and meaningful service Respect for the parent-child relationship 6.5 What Will Not Be Published Child names, addresses, case numbers, or private family facts Medical, school, financial, or court records Private attorney-client communications or screenshots Allegations about opposing parties or other attorneys Claims that an attorney guaranteed an outcome Claims that an attorney is the “best,” “top,” or superior to another attorney Negative reviews, accusations, disputes, or retaliatory comments 6.6 Publication Procedure A POPS Noted User submits a private Merit Recognition. POPS verifies the submitter's eligibility and first-hand relationship. POPS reviews the submission for privacy, truthfulness, and prohibited content. POPS may edit grammar, length, or identifying details without changing the intended meaning. POPS verifies public attorney information where reasonably possible. All published attorneys receive the same designation: POPS Noted Counsel - Merit Recognition. POPS may decline, revise, pause, or remove a recognition that is inaccurate, misleading, outdated, privacy-invasive, or inconsistent with this policy. 6.7 Attorney Participation Boundary Attorneys may not nominate themselves, pay for recognition, pay for placement, purchase visibility, or compensate POPS or POPS users for a commendation. Attorneys may request correction of public factual information or request removal of a profile, but they do not control the recognition standard. 7. Moderation and Enforcement POPS may restrict access, decline submissions, remove content, pause access, or terminate use when conduct threatens user safety, privacy, platform integrity, legal compliance, or the mission of POPS. POPS may remove content that contains private family information, unlawful material, fabricated claims, threats, harassment, misleading statements, prohibited evidence, or attempts to use POPS for revenge or retaliation. 8. Policy Updates POPS may update these policies as the product, security practices, reserve capacity, and operational requirements evolve. Material changes will be posted with a revised effective date. Continued use of POPS after an updated effective date means the user accepts the revised policy to the extent permitted by law.
